Because when you call `element.classList.remove()`, `this` = `element.classList`. The `_cls` is on `element`, not on `element.classList`. So `this._cls` = `classList._cls` = undefined. This is the SAME bug as before — a mock design flaw, NOT an app bug.

So both mocks are fundamentally broken for classList. My mock replicated the bug. I need to fix MY mock so `this._cls` resolves. The fix: define classList methods that close over the element's `_cls`, or put `_cls` on the classList object itself.
